sources.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018)
sources.locator: Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Definition 2.13 and Example 2.14; Proposition 2.20; Corollary 2.21; Theorem 2.22; Corollaries 2.23–2.24; Theorem 2.25; Theorem 2.26 and Corollary 2.27; §2.2.3 headings “Isometric and unitary channels” and “The completely dephasing channel”.

contents.name: Definition 2.13 — quantum channel
contents.support: The source defines a channel by complete positivity and trace preservation; the local definition fixes those conditions on the full finite operator space.

contents.name: Example 2.14 — unitary channels
contents.support: The example identifies unitary conjugation as a channel; the local proposition proves the claim for typed finite-dimensional spaces.

contents.name: Proposition 2.20 — equivalent map representations
contents.support: Its natural, Choi, Kraus, and Stinespring identities inform the local equivalence proof; the input-first convention is verified by direct matrix-unit computation.

contents.name: Corollary 2.21 — minimal Kraus and Stinespring dimensions
contents.reason: QC05 proves finite existence and a dimension upper bound, but does not claim minimal Choi-rank or minimal-environment results; that stronger rank theory is outside the assigned design.

contents.name: Theorem 2.22 — characterizations of completely positive maps
contents.support: This theorem treats complete positivity, Choi non-negativity, Kraus representations, and Stinespring forms; the assigned page proves its finite channel subset locally.

contents.name: Corollary 2.23 — unitary freedom of Kraus representations
contents.reason: The assigned page proves existence and equivalence of representations but makes no uniqueness or unitary-mixing claim about two Kraus families.

contents.name: Corollary 2.24 — unitary freedom of Stinespring representations
contents.reason: QC05 constructs a finite isometric dilation but does not classify when two dilations are equivalent or prove uniqueness up to an environment unitary.

contents.name: Theorem 2.25 — characterizations of Hermitian-preserving maps
contents.reason: Hermitian-preserving maps that need not be completely positive are not part of the assigned channel and representation scope.

contents.name: Theorem 2.26 — characterizations of trace-preserving maps
contents.support: The source gives the Choi partial-trace test; the local proof derives it in the declared input-first convention.

contents.name: Corollary 2.27 — characterizations of channels
contents.support: This channel characterization supports the four-way finite equivalence, whose separate local implications are assembled on the A page.

contents.name: §2.2.3 — isometric and unitary channels
contents.support: The source identifies isometric channels; the local proof gives the finite Kraus formula for partial trace and checks complete positivity and trace preservation.

contents.name: §2.2.3 — the completely dephasing channel
contents.support: The source gives the dephasing map and Kraus/Choi forms; the B page independently computes the qubit phase-flip family and its p=1/2 case.

sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3: Foundations II: Measurement and Evolution (PDF title page October 2018)
sources.locator: Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §§3.2.1, 3.2.6, 3.3.1–3.3.2: operator-sum representation, complete positivity, channel-state duality, and Stinespring dilation.

contents.name: §3.2.1 — the operator-sum representation
contents.support: The notes define channels by a finite operator sum, discuss composition, and obtain the local Kraus form; normalization and all-operator trace preservation are proved locally.

contents.name: §3.2.6 — complete positivity
contents.support: The notes define positivity under extension and show Kraus amplifications preserve positivity; the local proof uses the declared block convention.

contents.name: §3.2.6 — transpose as a positive map that is not completely positive
contents.reason: The assigned page characterizes completely positive maps and does not require a counterexample separating positivity from complete positivity; it makes no claim about the transpose map.

contents.name: §3.3.1 — channel-state duality
contents.support: The duality motivates the Choi/Kraus route; Preskill uses reference-first factors, while the local proof explicitly fixes and verifies input-first order.

contents.name: §3.3.1 — minimal Kraus count equals Choi rank
contents.reason: QC05 proves a finite Kraus family with a dimension upper bound but does not claim that the minimal number is the Choi rank.

contents.name: §3.3.1 — real parameter count for channels
contents.reason: Parameter counting is outside the assigned characterization and representation theorems and is not needed for any local proof.

contents.name: §3.3.2 — Stinespring dilation
contents.support: The notes construct an isometry from a Kraus family and recover the channel by tracing out the environment; the local proof verifies the coordinate formula.

contents.name: §3.3.2 — extension of an isometry to a unitary on a larger space
contents.reason: The local theorem asserts an isometric dilation only; it does not claim or need a unitary completion on an enlarged input space.

canonical.name: Adjoint identities for finite-dimensional linear isometries
canonical.support: Locally derived from the first-linear polarization formula, the adjoint identity, and nondegeneracy; it supplies the bridge V†V=I used by Stinespring proofs.

canonical.name: Tensor products of operator matrix units form a basis
canonical.support: Locally derived from product bases and coordinate columns; it makes the tensor channel map well-defined on the full operator space.

canonical.name: Global scalar phase invariance of one unitary conjugation map
canonical.support: Proved by direct adjoint algebra; the item explicitly makes no controlled-operation inference.

contents.name: §2.2.3 — the completely dephasing channel
contents.support: The source gives the dephasing action and Kraus/Choi/Stinespring representations; the local example computes the qubit phase-flip matrices and identifies p=1/2.

sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3: Foundations II: Measurement and Evolution (PDF title page October 2018)
sources.locator: Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3, §3.4.2, “Dephasing channel”, equations (3.97)–(3.101), PDF pp.27–28.

contents.name: §3.4.2 — dephasing channel, equations (3.97)–(3.101)
contents.support: Preskill computes a dephasing isometry, Kraus operators, and off-diagonal decay. Its parameter is a dephasing probability rather than the identity weight p used here; it independently supports the p=1/2 fully dephased case.
